subject: Coffee & Tea
title: The Enemies of Freshness
description: A fast breakdown of The Enemies of Freshness for builders.

hook.text: Four things destroy coffee freshness: oxygen, moisture, heat, and light. They work fast.

buildup.text: Oxygen triggers oxidation, breaking down the aromatic oils that give coffee its complex flavor.

discovery.text: Moisture causes staling and can introduce mold. Even humidity in the air accelerates degradation.

twist.text: Heat speeds every chemical reaction. Storing coffee near a stove is the single worst storage habit.

climax.text: An opaque, airtight container at room temperature is all you need. Simple, but most people skip it.

punchline.text: Four enemies, one solution: seal it, shade it, cool it.

quiz.question: What are the four enemies of coffee freshness?

details.summary: Coffee's flavor degrades through exposure to oxygen, moisture, heat, and light. Oxidation stales aromatic compounds within weeks of roasting. Proper storage in an airtight, opaque container at room temperature extends peak freshness to about a month for whole beans.
details.whyItMatters: Most coffee sold in supermarkets has already passed its peak. Understanding freshness helps consumers seek better coffee and store it properly.
takeaways: Oxygen is the primary enemy of coffee freshness
Whole beans stay fresh much longer than pre-ground coffee
Store in airtight, opaque containers at room temperature

faq.question: How long does coffee stay fresh after roasting?
faq.answer: Whole beans are best within 2 to 4 weeks of roasting. Pre-ground coffee starts losing flavor within hours. Sealed bags with one-way valves can extend shelf life to 2 to 3 months. Once opened, use within 2 weeks for best results.

faq.question: Should you store coffee in the refrigerator?
faq.answer: No. The refrigerator introduces moisture and odors that coffee readily absorbs. A cool, dark pantry in an airtight container is ideal. The freezer can work for long-term storage if the beans are sealed in airtight, single-use portions.
